current.text: He is a projected starter for Atlanta, next to CJ McCollum, Dyson Daniels, Jalen Johnson and Onyeka Okongwu.
Experts expect him to keep his starting spot. If Lu Dort starts, it would likely be in place of McCollum, not Alexander-Walker. That would give Alexander-Walker more shots and assists.
Trae Young is no longer with Atlanta, and the Hawks did not add anyone to replace him.
The conditions behind his rise are still in place. Kingston Flemings is not expected to start over him, and McCollum's extension delays Flemings further.

His shooting late last season (about 45 to 48% from three and about 95% at the line) will not hold. His role, minutes and time on the ball are expected to hold. Experts use his pre All-Star line (about 20 points, 58% true shooting) as the baseline, and that is still very good.
Expect his FT% to fall to about 81%, which would still be fine.
With McCollum on the roster for most of the season, his usage and ball handling should change.
He got more deflections in his bigger role and turned more of them into steals, so there may be room for more steals.

In category leagues, experts see him as a top 50 player. Lloyd says probably top 40. At an ADP in the 50s to 60s or in round 5, they call him good value and slightly undervalued. One expert calls him free money. Another calls an ESPN ADP of 115 indefensible.
In points leagues his value only matches his ADP, and pick 45 is too high there.
Experts value him in the mid 20s USD in auctions. In a mock auction, Josh got him for 14 USD.
Atlanta plays 4, 4 and 3 games in our playoff weeks 19 to 21 and has 14 back-to-backs. Resting players is not a concern, and the team did not shut players down last season.
Atlanta has no true point guard. Ball handling is shared among McCollum, Alexander-Walker, Johnson and Daniels.

durable.text: He has been one of the better catch-and-shoot three-point shooters in the NBA for three seasons. About 40% from three on high volume is a reasonable level for him.
His true free throw level is about 78 to 81%. Experts see his 90% last season as a random swing.
Quin Snyder runs an egalitarian, high-movement offense that wants many threes.

note: He is a bargain auction target. Yahoo values him at 18 USD and ESPN at 24 USD, but average costs are only 4.4 and 10.7 USD, and he went for 1 USD in our league last season. Experts call him a mid 20s USD player, so 12 to 18 USD is a good price and up to the low 20s is still fair. He has no weak category, so he fits any build, with threes, FT% and points as his main strengths. Early in the season, check how far his FT% and 3P% fall from last season's late run, and whether McCollum or Lu Dort cuts into his usage.
